CAR.head: The Hurricanes have a lot going for them
CAR.body: Even though Carolina may be without Ehlers, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Senators’ way back in is getting good looks.

OTT.head: A tough matchup for the Senators
OTT.body: Even though Carolina may be without Ehlers, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back. The Senators can pull it off if they get good looks.

story.head: Two of the best
paras: The Hurricanes have won three straight, and the Senators (17-7-3) beat Tampa Bay 6-2 last night. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Senators are first in the Atlantic (fourth in the NHL) and the Canes first in the Metropolitan (second).

The Senators’ record (.685) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.615), largely because they’re 8-3 in one-goal games. The Hurricanes’ record (.820) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd), keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd) and get into a lot of chippy games (3rd). As for the Hurricanes, they take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd), so the Senators keep dangerous shots away, but they give up a lot of them. Carolina has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.20, the fewest. Something has to give when the Hurricanes’ shooting runs into the Senators’ defense.

Tim Stützle (15 G / 18 A / 33 P in 27 GP) is carrying the Senators’ offense, with seven points in his last five games and six goals in nine games against Carolina since 2023-24. Sebastian Aho (13 G / 21 A / 34 P in 25 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.
Samuel Ersson (3-3-3 / .868 SV% in 8 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Ottawa, but will likely start. Pyotr Kochetkov (13-1-1 / .910 SV% in 15 GS) is in line to start for Carolina.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Kotkaniemi, Jankowski and Robinson out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Burakovsky, Halliday and Cousins.
